text: This computed trajectory shows that a spacecraft could reach the interstellar object 1I/'Oumuamua in about one year, departing Earth on June 7, 2017 and arriving at the object on June 7, 2018. The departure C₃ from Earth is 393.34 km²/s², which corresponds to a hyperbolic excess speed of 19.8328 km/s relative to Earth. When the spacecraft reaches 1I/'Oumuamua, its relative velocity with respect to the object will be 13.71605 km/s in the target-relative frame. The total flight time for this patched-conic, two-body trajectory is 365 days, or approximately one year.
verification_status: computed and validated against published figures (Hein et al. 2019)
